prompt: What did Marconi's 1901 transatlantic transmission carry?
explanation: Marconi's famous 1901 transmission from Poldhu to Newfoundland carried Morse code dots, not voice or music. Radio's earliest commercial use was as a wireless alternative to the wired telegraph for ship-to-shore communication and military signalling. Voice broadcasting was a 1920s development.

prompt: What did the first commercial broadcaster KDKA carry on its inaugural 1920 transmission?
explanation: KDKA Pittsburgh, the first commercially licensed broadcaster, went on the air in November 1920 with the Harding–Cox presidential election results. The political-news debut signalled the new medium's relationship with public life from the very start.

prompt: John Reith's mission for the BBC was to inform, _________, and entertain.
explanation: Reith's three-word mission codified the public-service-broadcasting tradition: inform, educate, and entertain. The order matters; in Reith's framing, entertainment was a means to deliver the first two purposes, not an end in itself. The doctrine still shapes BBC governance and public-service broadcasting policy across Europe and the Commonwealth.

prompt: Roosevelt's 'fireside chats' were politically powerful primarily because they:
options: Allowed FDR to bypass Republican-leaning newspaper publishers and address voters directly
Were broadcast only to wealthy households
correctAnswer: Allowed FDR to bypass Republican-leaning newspaper publishers and address voters directly
explanation: Roosevelt's thirty fireside chats (1933–1944) used radio's intimacy — a voice in your living room — to bypass the Republican-leaning newspaper publishers who controlled most US print media at the time. The first chat, on the 1933 banking crisis, drew an estimated 60-million-plus audience and pioneered an entire mode of broadcast political communication.

prompt: Match each early-radio figure to a contribution:

pairs.right: 1901 transatlantic wireless transmission of Morse code
Superheterodyne receiver patented 1918, basis for selective home radios
Live CBS Blitz broadcasts from London ('This is London')

explanation: These three figures span radio's first half-century. Marconi made the technology work at transatlantic distance; Armstrong's receiver design was what made home radio practical at scale; Murrow's wartime broadcasting set the standard for broadcast journalism that the medium has been measured against ever since.

prompt: Approximately what fraction of US households owned a television by 1960?
explanation: TV ownership rose from around 9% of US households in 1950 to 65% in 1955 and 87% in 1960. The post-war retooling of the wartime electronics industry produced one of the most rapid mass-medium adoption curves in history. Britain and Western Europe reached saturation a few years later.

prompt: The three commercial networks that dominated the US 'three-network era' were:
explanation: NBC, CBS, and ABC dominated US prime-time television from the 1950s through the 1980s. Fox launched as a fourth network in 1986; PBS was created by the 1967 Public Broadcasting Act as a non-commercial alternative; cable channels (HBO from 1972, CNN from 1980) followed later.

prompt: The TV ratings system that became the currency of US television advertising was created by Arthur C. _________.
explanation: Arthur C. Nielsen's company, founded for grocery-store sales measurement in the 1920s, applied similar techniques to radio audiences from 1942 and to television in the 1950s. The Nielsen ratings became — and largely remain — the industry-standard measurement of broadcast audiences in the United States.

prompt: After the 1968 Tet Offensive, what television figure's editorial assessment is reported to have prompted Lyndon Johnson to say 'If I've lost X, I've lost middle America'?
explanation: After CBS anchor Walter Cronkite returned from Vietnam in early 1968 and concluded the war was 'mired in stalemate' on a special report, Johnson reportedly told an aide, 'If I've lost Cronkite, I've lost middle America.' The episode is the standard illustration of broadcast journalism's mid-20th-century influence.

prompt: Match each landmark broadcast event to its significance:

pairs.right: First televised US presidential debate; appearance and demeanour now mattered
Four-day rolling coverage that made TV America's primary news medium
Largest global live audience to date; estimated 600 million worldwide viewers

explanation: These three events captured the medium's distinctive power during the broadcast era's peak. The Kennedy–Nixon debate showed how television transformed political performance. The assassination coverage demonstrated TV's capacity to make a national experience out of a single event. The moon landing drew the largest worldwide live audience yet assembled. None of these collective experiences has been quite reproducible in the post-broadcast environment.

prompt: What did the original CATV systems primarily do?
options: Use a tall hilltop antenna to redistribute existing broadcast signals to homes that couldn't receive them
correctAnswer: Use a tall hilltop antenna to redistribute existing broadcast signals to homes that couldn't receive them
explanation: Community Antenna Television began in the late 1940s as a way to bring existing broadcast signals to communities that could not receive them due to distance or terrain. CATV systems were redistribution networks; the shift to cable as a content medium in its own right came in the 1970s with HBO and the satellite-distribution era.

prompt: Which channel pioneered the 24-hour news format?
explanation: CNN — Cable News Network, launched June 1980 by Ted Turner — was the first 24-hour news channel. Its coverage of the 1991 Gulf War (with iconic live broadcast from Baghdad as bombing began) established the format and the 'CNN effect' that subsequent 24-hour news channels worldwide were modelled on.

prompt: The first music video aired on MTV in August 1981 was the Buggles' 'Video Killed the _____ Star.'
explanation: MTV launched on 1 August 1981 with the Buggles' 'Video Killed the Radio Star.' The choice was self-consciously symbolic of the new medium's challenge to broadcast radio. MTV's visual vernacular went on to reshape advertising, cinema, and the marketing of recorded music for a generation.

prompt: BSkyB's 1992 acquisition of which sporting rights drove its UK pay-TV growth and reshaped the economics of the sport?
explanation: Sky's exclusive deal for the newly-formed Premier League in 1992 made live English top-flight football a pay-TV product. The transformation of football's economics — vastly higher player wages, new stadium standards, global broadcasting rights — followed directly from the BSkyB rights deal. The same pattern of premium-sports-rights underwriting pay-TV emerged in many countries.

prompt: Match each cable-era channel to its launch year and category:

pairs.right: 1972 — first major satellite-distributed premium subscription channel
1981 — pioneered music video as a continuous broadcast format

explanation: These three channels redefined the categories in which they operated and established the cable-era business model. HBO proved subscription-funded premium channels were viable; ESPN demonstrated the power of single-genre channels; MTV created a visual vernacular that influenced media well beyond cable television itself.

prompt: What is the historical justification for stronger broadcast regulation than print regulation?
options: Spectrum scarcity — two stations on the same frequency in the same area destroy each other's signal
correctAnswer: Spectrum scarcity — two stations on the same frequency in the same area destroy each other's signal
explanation: Spectrum scarcity has been the legal foundation of broadcast regulation since the 1920s. The Supreme Court endorsed it in Red Lion (1969). The doctrine has been criticised in the cable and digital era when scarcity is much less acute, but has not been formally overturned and continues to underwrite a distinct broadcast First Amendment regime in the United States.

prompt: The Fairness Doctrine, repealed in 1987, required broadcast licensees to:
options: Devote reasonable airtime to controversial issues and reflect differing perspectives fairly
Carry equal advertising for all parties
correctAnswer: Devote reasonable airtime to controversial issues and reflect differing perspectives fairly
explanation: The Fairness Doctrine (1949–1987) required broadcasters to discuss controversial public-importance issues and to do so in a way that reflected differing viewpoints. Its 1987 repeal under FCC chairman Dennis Patrick is widely credited with enabling the rise of partisan talk radio and later partisan cable news.

prompt: The 1996 _________ Act dramatically liberalised US broadcast ownership rules and enabled rapid consolidation of radio and television.
explanation: The 1996 Telecommunications Act removed or eased single-owner caps on radio stations, raised television caps, and eased cross-media-ownership prohibitions. The result was rapid consolidation: Clear Channel acquired around 1,200 radio stations; Sinclair Broadcasting built up to nearly 200 local TV stations.

prompt: The British communications regulator, created in 2003 by combining several previous regulators, is:
explanation: Ofcom (the Office of Communications) was created in 2003 and combined the roles of several previous specialised regulators. It has powers covering broadcast television and radio, telecommunications, postal services, and (more recently) online safety. Its US counterpart is the FCC; BARB is the British audience-measurement body, not a regulator.

prompt: Match each US broadcast-regulation concept to its description:

pairs.right: Requires broadcasters offering airtime to one candidate to offer comparable time to opponents
Requires cable systems to carry local broadcast stations
Limit certain broadcast (not cable) content to designated hours

explanation: These three concepts are core elements of US broadcast policy. Equal-time rules manage political-campaign access. Must-carry rules ensure local-broadcaster carriage on cable systems. Indecency rules apply to broadcast but not to cable/streaming, illustrating the asymmetric regulatory treatment of broadcast versus subscription media that the digital era has further complicated.

prompt: A 'Nielsen rating point' in US television corresponds to roughly:
options: 1% of US households actually watching at the time
explanation: A rating point corresponds to roughly 1% of US TV households (whether or not the TV is on). A 'share point' corresponds to 1% of households actually using their televisions at the time. The two metrics are commonly reported together; the M*A*S*H finale's 60.2 rating with a 77 share is the historic peak for non-Super-Bowl scripted programming.

prompt: What are 'sweeps' in US broadcast television?
options: Four annual periods (Nov, Feb, May, Jul) Nielsen uses to set local-market ad rates
correctAnswer: Four annual periods (Nov, Feb, May, Jul) Nielsen uses to set local-market ad rates
explanation: The four sweeps periods each year had outsized importance because Nielsen used them to set local-market advertising rates. Networks loaded sweeps with their highest-rated programming, special episodes, and stunt programming designed to maximise demographic reach. The whole scheduling and promotion infrastructure of broadcast television was organised around the rhythm of measurement.

prompt: The British equivalent of Nielsen, established in 1981, is _________.
explanation: BARB (the Broadcasters' Audience Research Board) is a joint-industry body established 1981 that runs the metered-panel system measuring British television audiences. Most other countries have an equivalent: Médiamétrie (France), AGF (Germany), OzTAM (Australia).

prompt: Why has audience measurement become harder in the streaming era?
options: Streaming services are too small to measure
Streamers initially refused to share granular data, and audiences fragment across platforms (linear, streaming, TikTok, Reddit)
Streaming has fewer viewers than broadcast
correctAnswer: Streamers initially refused to share granular data, and audiences fragment across platforms (linear, streaming, TikTok, Reddit)
explanation: Streamers initially refused to share viewing data on the grounds that, as subscription services without ad-supported models, they did not need third-party measurement. Cross-platform measurement is harder still: a viewer might start a show on linear, finish on streaming, share clips on TikTok, and discuss on Reddit. The Nielsen ONE platform, VideoAmp, and ComScore xMedia are attempting to build a successor currency.

prompt: Match each measurement concept to its description:

pairs.right: Nielsen device installed in sample homes that recorded radio/TV station tuned
Sum of rating points delivered by an advertising schedule
Automatic content recognition on connected TVs that identifies what is playing

explanation: These three terms span six decades of audience-measurement technology. The Audimeter built mid-20th-century broadcast measurement; the GRP became the standard advertising currency built on top of it; ACR is one of the modern technologies through which Nielsen and competitors measure streaming and connected-TV viewing in the post-broadcast environment.

prompt: Approximately when did US pay-TV subscriptions peak before cord-cutting began?
explanation: US pay-TV subscriptions peaked at around 100 million households around 2010 and have fallen steadily since, reaching under 60 million by 2024. The pace of decline accelerated after 2018 as streaming services became credible substitutes for cable's most-watched content while leaving expensive sports and news rights in place.

prompt: Which Netflix original series, released in 2013, is widely cited as marking Netflix's transition into a major content producer?
explanation: House of Cards (2013), Netflix's first major original series, demonstrated that the streaming platform could compete with traditional networks for prestige programming. Its data-driven commissioning (Netflix used viewership data to identify the appetite for political drama with David Fincher and Kevin Spacey) became part of the Netflix mythology.

prompt: The free ad-supported streaming TV tier (with services like Tubi, Pluto TV, Roku Channel) is abbreviated _________.
explanation: FAST (free ad-supported streaming television) services emerged in the 2020s as a streaming counterpart to broadcast television. Tubi, Pluto TV, the Roku Channel, and Samsung TV Plus offer linear-style channels and on-demand content funded by advertising rather than subscription. The model has grown rapidly as streaming economics have settled.

prompt: How many monthly users does YouTube reach globally?
explanation: YouTube reaches over 2.5 billion monthly users globally. Its watch-time exceeds the major streamers combined for many demographic segments, and the platform has become the dominant single video destination on connected televisions in many markets — even though it is rarely thought of as a streaming service in the traditional sense.

prompt: Match each post-broadcast platform or programme to a description:

pairs.right: Long-form interview podcast signed to Spotify in $200M deal in 2020
User-generated video platform acquired by Google in 2006; dominant on connected TVs

explanation: These three illustrate distinct post-broadcast formats: long-form independent shows funded by sponsorship and platform revenue (Rogan), subscription streaming services with traditional production budgets (Netflix), and user-generated platforms operating at vast scale (YouTube). Together they have replaced most of what broadcast television once delivered, with very different economics and audience-relationship structures.
